correctness.rationale: Independently computed symbolic Lie derivative of the exact quartic under the published Filiptsov vector field; it factors as cofactor times quartic, matching arXiv:2210.15803 Case 3. Setting X=a²x, Y=a²y, z=Y/X and s=1+a gives quadratic 3s X²−2 z h_a(z) X+3s a² z²=0 with h_a=3sz−2z²−3sa. The discriminant gives exact z interval and two roots X± with product a²z². The Jacobian of (X,z)↦(X,zX) is X, so scaled area a^4 A= (2/(9s²))∫ z² h_a sqrt(h_a²−(3sa)²) dz. Uniform error bound 0<=h²−h sqrt(h²−d²)<=d² across the admissible interval yields O(a²), and endpoint shifts contribute higher order O(a³). Independent exact rational polynomial integration gives leading 81/560 and linear −81/280, yielding displayed asymptotic. Uniform outer-root and inner-root collapse prove Hausdorff convergence; differentiating limiting X0 and Y0 gives maxima 2/3, 729/1024. These are universal asymptotic arguments, not extrapolations of the finite quadrature diagnostic.
residual_risks: Unverified publisher/Lean/expert certification is not asserted; exact scope is only the stated hypothesis.

final_claim: For Filiptsov quadratic family, 0<a<3/13, the known positive oval has Euclidean area A(a)=81/(560a^4)-81/(280a^3)+O(a^-2). Under (x,y)↦(a²x,a²y) it converges in Hausdorff distance to the explicit singular Jordan loop ((2/3)z²(3-2z),(2/3)z³(3-2z)), 0<=z<=3/2, whose maximal X and Y are 2/3 and 729/1024.
